newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Higher EU steel output boosts Jan world production.
newsitem.headline: Higher EU steel output boosts Jan world production.

text.p: World steel production rose 3.7 percent to 61.9 million tonnes in January year-on-year, partly due to better figures for western Europe and Asia, the International Iron and Steel Institute said on Wednesday.
January crude steel output rose 5.6 percent to 13.8 million tonnes in western Europe and eight percent to 24 million tonnes in Asia, IISI said in a statement.
"As their economies continue to improve, most of the major steel producing countries in the European Union are showing a return to higher steel production levels," IISI said.
Compared with January last year, production jumped 14.8 percent, 12.0 percent and 10.4 percent respectively in Britain, Germany and France.
"As in the past months, the exception was once again Italy, where production fell by 13.1 percent to 1.9 million tonnes," IISI said.
However, production in eastern Europe fell 7.1 percent, partly due to a 22.9 percent drop in Poland. Output in the former Soviet Union was 2.9 percent lower at 5.7 million tonnes.
Strikes and other unexpected outages brought production in North America down 1.3 percent to 10.4 million tonnes.
